title: Contract error envelope (v1)
x-why: A bare message string cannot be switched on, cannot be counted, and cannot be told apart from another error with similar wording -- which is how two different failures end up in one bucket. Every error crossing the boundary answers three questions: whose problem it is, whether it is terminal, and what is still true.

code.description: Namespaced by owner. The namespace and the owner field must agree; a mismatch means an internal limitation being transmitted as an external blocker, or the reverse.

owner.description: EXTERNAL waits on somebody else's published repository. INTERNAL is work in this project. CONTRACT is the boundary itself being wrong -- a version mismatch, a schema violation, a field this reader has never heard of -- and is the only one of the three fixed by changing the contract.

terminal.description: A terminal error is an answer. A non-terminal one is a step that failed and may be retried. Reporting a retryable failure as terminal inflates the count of finished entries.

established.description: Three-state facts that survived the failure. An error does not erase the gates measured before it, and a consumer should not have to treat a late failure as though nothing had been measured.
